clue.text: Flask with its top in position-it maintains temperature

parts.note: a Thermos is a vacuum flask
the top, or first letter, of the flask's name, Thermos, is T
to be at a place is to be in position there

explanation.surface: A vacuum flask with its stopper in place keeps a drink hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its top' points back at the flask: the first letter of THERMOS supplies the extra T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is the device that regulates heat, keeping a room or appliance at a set level.

clue.text: Pastry begins crumbling at edges

indicators.note: crumbling at the edges means losing the outer letters, so both ends of the synonym fall away

parts.note: begins means starts

explanation.surface: A pie crust starts to fall apart around its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begins' gives STARTS; 'crumbling at edges' removes its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling.

clue.text: Place for show, formerly, on Italian river

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-husband
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: An old exhibition site on the banks of a river in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition, a venue where goods are put on display.

clue.text: Devious animal I've put out

indicators.note: out here means not in its usual order, so the letters of animal I've put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cunning creature has been released by me.
explanation.definitionFit: A manipulative person controls others by deceit, so devious describes them.

clue.text: Went a length of the way with one Hindu mentor

parts.words: Went a length of the way
parts.note: swimming a length of a pool means travelling its whole distance, so went a length is swam
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guru walked part of the road alongside one pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests walking; the length is a length of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a spiritual guide to followers.

clue.text: Boozy call Ohio chap at first scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of call Ohio are put into a new order
at first takes only the opening letter of the word chap

explanation.surface: A drunk phones a man in Ohio, all muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' turns CALL OHIO into ALCOHOLI; 'at first' adds C from 'chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic means containing or relating to liquor, so a boozy drink fits.

clue.text: Finish putting back crockery

indicators.note: putting something back here means writing the crockery word from its end to its start

parts.note: pots are pieces of crockery

explanation.surface: Someone stops work by putting the dishes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting back' turns POTS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something is to bring it to a halt, a verb synonym.

clue.text: After bit of turnip, eat carrot shredded-it's a sort of orange colour

indicators.note: after says the anagram comes after the turnip letter
a bit of the word turnip here is just its first letter
shredded vegetables are cut up, so the letters of eat carrot are jumbled

explanation.surface: Grate a carrot after a piece of turnip, and the colour is orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes T from 'turnip'; 'shredded' rearranges EAT CARROT into ERRACOTTA; 'After' puts that behind the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a brownish-orange shade, named after the fired clay of that tint.

clue.text: High point for party member after first day of week

indicators.note: after says the party member comes after the day abbreviation

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
Mon, short for Monday, is taken as the week's first day
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A peak for a party politician after Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland, land jutting high into the sea.

clue.text: Being sorry about writer can't upset anyone ultimately

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of can't are thrown into a new order
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of anyone is taken

explanation.surface: Contrition over an author who can't upset anybody at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges CANT into TANC; 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of 'anyone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is the state of feeling regret for wrongdoing, so being sorry describes it.

clue.text: Spirit shown by bachelor at carnival venue

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
Rio de Janeiro is famous for its annual carnival

explanation.surface: A single man shows plenty of zest at the carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vivacity or verve, the same lively quality as spirit.

clue.text: Produce talking books?

parts.note: read literally, to utter books aloud is to produce talking books; the idiom means to be highly revealing

explanation.surface: Publishing audiobooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to say a great deal without words; read literally, it is volumes that talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a book, and talking books are volumes that speak, matching the idiom read word by word.

clue.text: Joanna definitely not grand?

parts.note: Joanna is rhyming slang for a keyboard instrument, and one that is not a grand is the other main kind, standing tall rather than lying flat

explanation.surface: A woman called Joanna is far from grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' is Cockney rhyming slang for piano; 'not grand' means not a grand piano, and 'upright' also plays on honest or plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Any piano that is not a grand is typically the vertical upright type found in homes.

clue.text: Imam's tunic decorated with medals

definitions.note: the adjective means concerned with coins and medals, so with medals stands for it

indicators.note: decorated suggests something being adorned and reworked, so the letters of Imam's tunic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious leader's robe is adorned with decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorated' looks like the medals' action, but it signals the anagram of IMAMS TUNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Numismatics is the study and collecting of coins and medals, so the adjective relates to them.

clue.text: Stridency? Quiet's needed by king with malady

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a malady is an illness

explanation.surface: A sick king demands silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridency is a harsh, piercing quality of sound, the same as a high piercing tone.

clue.text: Messing up fun he'll appear obstructive

indicators.note: messing things about jumbles them, so the letters of up fun he'll are rearranged

explanation.surface: If he spoils the fun, he will look awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing' looks like it pairs with 'up' as a phrasal verb, but 'up' is part of the fodder: UP FUN HELL rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obstructive means getting in the way rather than giving any assistance.

clue.text: Entertainment, with church hosting dance? No such thing!

indicators.note: hosting means holding inside, so the entertainment word holds the dance word

parts.note: fun is entertainment
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A church social with dancing is advertised as costing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' puts REEL inside FUN. The definition alludes to the saying 'there's no such thing as a free lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that nothing comes without cost, so this gratis meal is the thing that does not exist.

clue.text: Take on promotion-work tirelessly at first

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a promotion
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word tirelessly

explanation.surface: Accept a promotion and labour without rest from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child, policy or idea is to take it on as your own.

clue.text: Fool one with a point about current

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the point word goes round the current symbol

parts.note: a dot is a small point
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A clown with a sharp remark about the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DOT around I to make DIOT, after the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, one who behaves foolishly.

clue.text: digger

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'digger (9)': the clue is cut short, with only its definition left and no wordplay; no scan or reprint gives the rest.

clue.text: With evil intent, men levy a toll that's unjust

indicators.note: something unjust is not right or fair, so the letters of men levy a toll are put into another order

explanation.surface: Officials impose an unfair toll out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unjust' rearranges MEN LEVY A TOLL; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is ill will, so acting this way means acting out of a wish to harm.

clue.text: Stair post in stone, well-constructed

indicators.note: in shows the letters are held within the words stone, well-constructed

explanation.surface: A banister support set into well-made stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'stoNE WELl'; 'constructed' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the upright post at the foot or turn of a staircase.

clue.text: Indigo hidden by vanilla

indicators.note: hidden by says the letters are concealed inside the word vanilla

explanation.surface: A blue dye lurks in a vanilla pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Grey, like a tree when burnt?

explanation.surface: A burnt tree turns grey.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the ash tree and on the ashes left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured means pale grey; and a tree burnt to ashes, or an ash tree, is ash-like.

clue.text: Ready to strike, of course, as mentioned in late edition

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words late edition, running across them

explanation.surface: Something is said to be ready for publication in the final edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a golf course: a ball on its peg is ready to be struck. The letters run across 'laTE EDition'.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a ball placed on a tee is set up and ready for the player's stroke.

clue.text: Shared idea could be far from decisive

explanation.surface: A joint notion might well be indecisive.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally: an idea held by two people is in two minds at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a thought held by a pair of people; idiomatically, the phrase means undecided or wavering between options.

clue.text: Thrown about on street

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Something tossed around in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast is the past participle of the verb meaning to throw or fling.

clue.text: Peter Pan?

parts.note: Barrie's story of the boy who never grew up is a stage drama written for youngsters, so it is a play belonging to the young

explanation.surface: Just the name of the boy who never grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means something very easy; here it is read literally as a drama for youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is a stage show for youngsters, literally a drama of the kind meant for the young.
